Bowler Wine
NYC Wine Spirits Importer Distributor
About Us
About Us Collage
The Company
Bowler is an independent, family-owned fine wine and spirits distributor and importer based in New York City.  At Bowler you'll find a portfolio made up of mostly small, family run estates-- most of whom share a philosophy that includes organic or biodynamic farming practices and winemaking or distilling techniques best described as low intervention.
While we acknowledge the importance of place, or terroir, in winemaking and distilling, our emphasis has always been on the people behind the product; the growers, the winemakers and the distillers. To us, where a wine comes from and what grape is used are less important than who is making it; their philosophy, their taste and their approach.
It is our goal to provide excellent service by a knowledgeable and professional staff, and to run the company in a way that values our employees and our customers.

results.rawContent:
Welcome to De Maison Selections
A Curated World of Wine, Spirits, and Ciders
Wines of integrity, stories with soul
De Maison Selections is the exclusive US importer of exceptional, artisanal properties from Spain, France, Japan, and beyond, which are rooted in their land and demonstrate respect for their ecology and heritage. As a result, our releases are imbued with a unique cultural stamp and authenticity.
It is this originality of identity and commitment to sustainability which drives the next generation of independent artisans. Innovation and bettering the status quo are at the core of our philosophy.
“Del most flor, amb la dedicació i el rigor de l’obra artesanal ben feta.”
This Catalan saying that graces the label of the first wine we imported, Avinyó Cava, translates to:“Starting with the best part of the harvest, and exerting the dedication and rigor of a well-crafted work.”  
It has guided the direction of our company since 1996. We believe that respecting the integrity of the source material with care and intention leads to deeper cultural connection, better wine, and lasting relationships.
Introducing the Porróncast: Voices from Vine to Glass
The Porróncast is our podcast series that brings you the stories of winemakers, distillers, restaurateurs, and creatives who share the Porrón, and what drives their passion for their craft. Hosted by Ryan Looper, with frequent appearances by other members of the De Maison team, each episode brings you inside the minds shaping the future of our industry.
Live from Pass the Porrón: The Gold Coast of Rioja & Reclaiming Place with André Tamers
October 9, 2026
This panel discussion was recorded live during
Pass the Porrón, De Maison’s 30th birthday celebration, on Friday, April 24th 2026.Can a famous wine region reinvent itself without losing its audience?
In this live panel discussion led by De Maison Selections founder André Tamers, we explore the changing landscape of Rioja as it transitions from traditional brand-driven consistency toward site-specificity, terroir, and wines of place. Joined by four independent grower-producers from the De Maison portfolio, André tackles one of the biggest questions in the wine world today: When a region’s commercial success is built on a uniform, recognizable identity, how do you reframe the narrative around quality and origin without leaving consumers behind?
The panel goes deep on why Rioja is often misunderstood, and why place and village identity is the clearest path forward, engaging with topics like: time versus place, how labeling rules shape what you see on a bottle, and what has to change for small producers to survive and thrive.
In this episode, the panel covers:
Terroir vs. Aging: How traditional aging classifications can flatten diversity, and why Reserva and Gran Reserva can coexist with village wines when terroir leads the story.
Village Microclimates: How limestone soils drive acidity in Samaniego whites, altitude brings freshness to Labastida, and river-influenced terraces shape San Vicente.
Rethinking Oak: The role of oak as a complementary tool rather than the dominant flavor profile.
Industry Action: What importers, retailers, and educators must do as Rioja portfolios become more granular and place-focused.
Guest Panel:
Pablo Rodríguez of Remelluri
Alain Quintana representing the Cosecheros de Labastida
Maríasun Saenz de Samaniego from Ostatu
Carlos Yécora of Luberri

Gavi and Vallee d'Aoste Featured in Wine Enthusiast
Gavi and Vallee d’Aoste – two unsung heroes of Italian wine regions that RWM has long celebrated – recently received their flowers with features in Wine Enthusiast.
Read more
 

Events & Press
Chateaus Simone and Pradeaux Receive Overdue Praise
Though iconic in the opinion of some, the wine of Provence’s Chateaus Simone and Pradeaux have always flown under the radar of critics and, therefore, the larger fine wine market. That is no longer the case as overdue praise emerges for Provence and, specifically, two of our longest standing partners in the region.

Events & Press
Carema’s Evolution: A Conversation with Neal Rosenthal & Vinous's Antonio Galloni
Piedmont holds a special place in Rosenthal Wine Merchant’s history: the very first wine Neal ever purchased for import was the legendary Carema from the Ferrando family, in the Alpine foothills of the region’s northwest corner. In conversation with Vinous’s Antonio Galloni, Neal leads an illuminating discussion on Nebbiolo to reflect upon its past, its changing landscape, and the traditions that continue to shape its future.

Grower Spotlights
Clementi 2007 Amarone Riserva
In truly exceptional vintages, Clementi produces a staggering Amarone Riserva which they age for a minimum of ten years in barrel, followed by at least five years in bottle. To date, they have produced such a wine only in 2007, 2009, and 2015, and we are thrilled to debut the 2007 Amarone Riserva into our portfolio this spring—an eye-popping 19 years after it was harvested.

Grower Spotlights
New Releases from Gravner: Spring 2026
It is no exaggeration to count Josko Gravner among the most influential winegrowers of the past half-century, and in the world of low-intervention wine his impact is perhaps unmatched. Gravner’s revival of the ancient practices of white-wine skin-maceration and subterranean amphorae in the early 2000s was a bold rejection of technology’s ever-increasing role in the winemaking process, and it is a testament to his vision, skill, and tenacity that he experienced such resounding success in light of such a radical reimagining of purpose.
